title: Police Union Executive Imported Thousands of Opioid Pills — Then Received Probation
subtitle: Joanne Segovia — San Jose Police Officers' Association opioid importation case
description: A source-backed examination of Joanne Segovia's years-long overseas opioid shipment history, the government's correction of the original fentanyl allegation, her guilty plea to unlawfully importing tapentadol, and the sentencing record that resulted in probation rather than incarceration.
keyPoints: The 2023 complaint alleged a long history of overseas pill shipments.
Segovia pleaded guilty in October 2024 to unlawfully importing tapentadol.
The original fentanyl-related charge was removed after prosecutors acknowledged a testing error.
Judge Eumi K. Lee imposed three years of probation and 100 hours of community service with no prison term.
investigativeAngles: How addiction, rehabilitation, deception, institutional position, and individualized federal sentencing were weighed in the final outcome.
How to distinguish institutional oversight questions from unsupported claims of broader organizational criminal participation.
